n=ell+1. Index sets below are I_n={0,...,ell}, equivalently Fin n. In scalar expressions ell−2i is integer subtraction.
For every natural r, X(r)=X_r=(r!:C)^(-1) x^r. Here 0!=1 and the zeroth operator power is Id_V.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of U(sl2(C)) acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is exactly the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra generated by every divided power x^r/r! and y^r/r! for natural r; its represented generators on V are X_r,Y_r.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, with K-scalar action on the second tensor factor. Tensor products are algebraic, generated additively by pure tensors subject to additivity and Z-balancing.
U=K⊗_Z M, with K-scalar action on the first tensor factor.

For f∈End_Z(M), define the K-linear operator F(f) by F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). The rule is additive and Z-balanced in a,m, so the tensor universal property defines an additive operator, and multiplication on the first factor makes it K-linear. This defines a function, with its ring-homomorphism laws to be proved separately.
S(m⊗a)=a⊗m, extended additively by the tensor universal property: the displayed rule is additive in each input and Z-balanced. K-linearity and bijectivity are proved internally.
S_inv(a⊗m)=m⊗a, defined by the same additive Z-balanced universal property.
ind(f) is the induced lattice operator on V_K, given by ind(f)(m⊗a)=f(m)⊗a. The additive Z-balanced rule defines the operator and is K-linear by the scalar action on the second factor.

argument.text: H003 gives lambda=(ell:Z), so H004 gives dim_C V=n=ell+1. Choose the common integer/complex basis bZ,bC indexed by I from H007. Apply M008 over C to bC: C is nontrivial, and finite-dimensional V is finitely generated, so I is finite. Apply M009 to the same basis: |I|=dim_C V=n. Thus this arbitrary original basis can be reindexed by Fin(n); no specially scaled highest-weight basis of M is assumed.

argument.text: Choose beta:Fin(n)→I using F001 and let mBasis be the reindexed Z-basis of M. Its images are still a complex basis. Use the canonical baseChange(K) basis qBasis. For arbitrary idx∈Fin(n), M002 identifies qBasis_idx=1⊗mBasis_idx in U=K⊗_Z M. The structure conditions hold because Z is a commutative ring, K has its integer algebra structure, and M is a Z-module. M005 gives dim_K U=|Fin(n)|=n. Here fields have the strong rank condition, the usual invariant-basis-number consequence of linear independence. Since n=ell+1>0, the index 0 exists. qBasis_0≠0: its own basis coordinate at 0 is 1≠0 in K. Thus U≠0.

argument.text: The K,M,F names in E001's verbatim source statement are source-bound (their ledger aliases are k0,M0,G0). Apply E001 with its source field/module instantiated by the problem K,M, giving a unital ring homomorphism G with G(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). This is the same pure-tensor formula as D020 F. For each f, both G(f) and F(f) are additive maps, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so they agree everywhere. Thus F=G as functions and F itself preserves 1, multiplication, 0 and addition. In particular finite sums, powers, negative operators and integer multiples are preserved. This identifies the prepared adapter with the actual operators used here.

produces.statement: F is a unital ring homomorphism End_Z(M)→End_K(U), with F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m) for every f,a,m.

argument.text: The formulas defining S,S_inv are additive in each input and Z-balanced: for an integer t, the tensor relation a⊗(t m)=(t a)⊗m verifies that moving t between the inputs gives the same value, and the reversed tensor relation verifies this for S_inv. Thus the additive tensor maps are well-defined. For any b,a∈K and m∈M, S(b·(m⊗a))=S(m⊗ba)=ba⊗m=b·S(m⊗a); the same calculation proves K-linearity of S_inv. Their composites fix every pure tensor and hence every finite sum of pure tensors. They are therefore mutual inverses. From F002, U≠0; the isomorphism S then gives V_K≠0.

produces.statement: S:V_K→U is a K-linear isomorphism with inverse S_inv, and V_K≠0.

argument.text: Fix f0 and a pure tensor m0⊗a0. By the defining formulas, S(ind(f0)(m0⊗a0))=S(f0(m0)⊗a0)=a0⊗f0(m0)=F(f0)(S(m0⊗a0)). Equality extends to every tensor by additivity. Thus S ind(f0)=F(f0) S for every f0. If a subspace is invariant under ind(f0), its image under S is invariant under F(f0); conversely use S_inv. The inverse identities also send zero and whole spaces to zero and whole spaces. With F002,F003,F004 this proves the full scalar-extension, dimension and intertwining statement.
